subproblem.title: A.e. Jacobian identity on a C¹ antilipschitz chart of a rectifiable triple
subproblem.statement: Assume (S1) ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} for all P, n and all v : Fin n → ℝ^P, and (S2) simpleNVector(i ↦ Σ_j B_ij τ_j) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ for all P, n, all real n×n matrices B and all τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (this conjunction is verbatim the frozen type of the already-reserved theorem lpf_simple_nvector_algebra; it is taken as a hypothesis so that this lemma is provable independently and the parent discharges it with Submission.lpf_simple_nvector_algebra). Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q), Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P C¹ and c-antilipschitz on Ω for some c > 0, and suppose that for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M), range DΦ(w) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at Φ(w) and f∘Φ has Fréchet derivative L(Φ(w))∘DΦ(w) at w. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M): ‖L(Φ(w))_#ξ(Φ(w))‖ₑ·JΦ(w) = J(f∘Φ)(w) in [0,∞], where JΦ(w) = √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩) and J(f∘Φ)(w) = √det(⟨D(f∘Φ)(w)e_i, D(f∘Φ)(w)e_j⟩) (both embedded by ENNReal.ofReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), ‖simpleNVector v‖ ^ 2 = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)).det) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), simpleNVector (fun i => ∑ j, B i j • τ j) = B.det • simpleNVector τ) → ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → (∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (Φ w) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap) ∧ HasFDerivAt (f ∘ Φ) ((L (Φ w)).comp (fderiv ℝ Φ w)) w) → ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), ‖nVectorPushforward n (L (Φ w)) (ξ (Φ w))‖ₑ * ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det) = ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))).det)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is steps 2–3 of the parent proof (good parameters and the Jacobian identity J(x)·JΦ_j(w) = Ju_j(w)) for one chart; the chain-rule hypothesis is exactly the conclusion of the frozen theorem lpf_chart_chain_rule, which the parent supplies.

1. (S is null-measurable.) S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M). M is Hⁿ-null-measurable (IsRectifiableTriple.nullMeasurableSet); choose a Borel B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0. Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) is Borel (Φ is continuous, being C¹, and Ω is open), and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B) is Lⁿ-null by the sibling lemma chart_preimage_null. S is their union, hence Lⁿ-null-measurable.
2. (Transfer of orients.) Let G be the set of x ∈ ℝ^P for which there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P such that span(range τ) is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x and ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. The field orients of IsRectifiableTriple says Hⁿ⌞M(Gᶜ) = 0 (ae_iff); as M is null-measurable, Hⁿ⌞M(Gᶜ) = Hⁿ(Gᶜ ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply₀'), so Hⁿ(Gᶜ ∩ M) = 0. By chart_preimage_null, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Gᶜ ∩ M)) = 0. Hence for Lⁿ-a.e. w, w ∈ S implies Φ(w) ∈ G. Since Lⁿ⌞S ≪ Lⁿ (ae_restrict_of_ae) and Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w lies in S (ae_restrict_mem₀, step 1), Φ(w) ∈ G for Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w.
3. (Good parameters.) Intersecting the a.e. sets of the hypothesis, of step 2 and of ae_restrict_mem₀: for Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w we have w ∈ S, Φ(w) ∈ G, (i) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (Φ w) (range DΦ(w)) and (ii) HasFDerivAt (f∘Φ) (L(Φ w)∘DΦ(w)) w. Fix such a w and put x := Φ(w).
4. (Uniqueness of the tangent plane.) x ∈ M, so θ(x) > 0 (IsRectifiableTriple.pos) and θ(x) ≠ 0. Let τ witness x ∈ G. By uniqueness of weighted approximate tangent spaces at points of nonzero multiplicity (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), range DΦ(w) = span(range τ); in particular DΦ(w)v ∈ span(range τ) for every v (LinearMap.mem_range_self).
5. (Linear algebra.) Apply the sibling lemma jacobian_identity (passing it the assumed (S1) ∧ (S2)) with A := DΦ(w), τ, ξ := ξ(x) and L := L(x): ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖·JΦ(w) = √det(⟨L(x)DΦ(w)e_i, L(x)DΦ(w)e_j⟩).
6. (Chain rule.) By (ii), fderiv ℝ (f∘Φ) w = L(x)∘DΦ(w) (HasFDerivAt.fderiv), and (L(x)∘DΦ(w))e_i = L(x)(DΦ(w)e_i) (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply); so the right side of step 5 is J(f∘Φ)(w).
7. (Passing to [0,∞].) ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖ (ofReal_norm) and ofReal(a)·ofReal(b) = ofReal(a·b) for a ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul); hence ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖ₑ·ofReal(JΦ(w)) = ofReal(‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖·JΦ(w)) = ofReal(J(f∘Φ)(w)). This holds for Lⁿ⌞S-a.e. w. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable (Borel part plus chart_preimage_null).
orients holds at Φ(w) for a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) (Hⁿ-null exceptional set pulled back by chart_preimage_null).
θ(Φ w) > 0 and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique give range DΦ(w) = span τ.
jacobian_identity with A = DΦ(w), L = L(Φ w); HasFDerivAt.fderiv identifies D(f∘Φ)(w) = L(Φ w)∘DΦ(w).
Convert to [0,∞] with ofReal_norm and ENNReal.ofReal_mul.

audit.reason: Exact contract match, including global C¹ regularity and the assumed a.e. chain rule. Null pullbacks transfer orientation to parameters; membership in M supplies θ > 0 for tangent uniqueness.
